newsitem.title: USA: PG&E found liable in toxic fumes suit.
newsitem.headline: PG&E found liable in toxic fumes suit.

text.p: A San Jose, Calif., jury ruled Tuesday against PG&E Corp, ordering the utility to pay $30 million for failing to investigate 1989 complaints of toxic fumes at an office building which endangered a pregnant woman who worked there.
The suit was brought by Cynthia Behr, who later gave birth to a brain-damaged baby.
The jury found PG&E negligent for not addressing the complaints as well as liable for fraud.
The utility said it will ask the presiding judge to either set the verdict aside or lower the award. Failing either of those actions, the company plans to appeal the verdict.
PG&E said in a statement its employees "acted professionally and properly with regard to this case."
The utility said it was sued only because all of the other parties in the case had reached out-of-court settlements.
